BiblicalUsage: Ga'ayon is the haughty one, the proud man at ease. The psalmist complains in Psalms 123:4 that his soul is filled with the scorning of those at ease and the contempt of the proud. The word appears only here, in a prayer of a people worn down by the scorn of the comfortable.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God hears the prayer of the scorned; the proud at ease may fill our souls with contempt, but the psalm turns straight to the LORD, and I hold that He lifts His eyes to the afflicted.
